issues.title: var used instead of const
issues.description: The rule requires that all variable declarations use let or const instead of var, but var was used to declare the newValues variable
issues.rule_name: Code Must Use let or const Instead of var

issues.title: Race condition: search input cleared synchronously causes visual glitch
issues.description: The handleClose function was modified to clear the search input synchronously using setSearchInput('') instead of the debounced setTimeout(() => setSearchInput(''), 200). This creates a race condition where the search input is cleared while the popover closing animation is still running, causing a visible flash where the filtered results disappear before the popover closes. The original implementation used a 200ms delay to allow the popover animation to complete before clearing the search state, preventing visual artifacts. This bug affects user experience by showing jarring UI state changes during the transition.

issues.title: Missing handleClose call in single-select mode prevents search input cleanup
issues.description: In the unselected options section for single-select mode, the code calls setOpen(false) but fails to call handleClose(), unlike the multiselect path which properly calls handleClose() when autoCloseOnSelect is enabled. This means when a user selects a single option, the popover closes but the search input state is never cleared, causing the next time the popover opens to show stale search results and filtered options from the previous interaction. The handleClose() function is responsible for clearing the search input and triggering the onClose callback, both of which are now skipped in single-select scenarios.

issues.title: Memory leak: temporary selected values not cleared on filter popover close
issues.description: The onClose handler in the SelectOptionsPopover component was modified to remove the setTempSelectedValues([]) cleanup call. This causes a memory leak where tempSelectedValues state persists after the popover closes. When a user opens the add filter popover, selects a field that supports options, starts selecting values, then closes the popover without confirming, those temporary values remain in state. If the user then opens a different field's options, they may see incorrect pre-selected values carried over from the previous interaction. The original PR correctly added this cleanup in line 2102 to ensure temporary state is cleared, but this bug removes it causing state pollution across different filter field selections.

issues.title: autoCloseOnSelect fails to close popover in non-inline multiselect mode
issues.description: The autoCloseOnSelect feature was implemented inconsistently across inline and non-inline modes. In non-inline Popover mode (line 1135-1137), when a multiselect option is selected with autoCloseOnSelect enabled, the code only calls onClose?.() without calling setOpen(false). Since SelectOptionsPopover can be instantiated without an onClose prop (line 1598), the optional chaining results in a no-op, leaving the popover open despite user selection. This breaks the intended UX where the dropdown should close immediately after selection when autoCloseOnSelect is configured. The inline mode implementation (line 1272-1273) correctly calls handleClose() which performs both operations.

issues.title: Double-quoted string literal used in JSX attribute
issues.description: Rule requires single quotes for string literals. The updated JSX uses a double-quoted string for the className attribute in the modified line.
issues.problematic_code_snippet: <div className="flex items-center self-stretch border border-r-[0px] px-3 text-sm text-muted-foreground">
issues.rule_name: Code Must Use Single Quotes for Strings

pr.title: Code Review Bench PR #25574 - Analytics filter refinements

structured_output.summary:
This PR polishes the Stats analytics filter bar. In the shared shade `Filters` component it adds an opt-in `autoCloseOnSelect` field flag, a `self-stretch` operator box, a `sm` size padding tweak, popover width/animation overrides, and clears the search query when a select popover closes. In the Stats app it makes the audience field a hidden-operator multiselect that auto-closes, switches the Post icon, hides option icons on UTM/source chips, restyles the count badges, and replaces the add-filter button with an icon-only `FunnelPlus` button. It also adjusts the sticky header padding.

Most of the intent is clear and the opt-in `autoCloseOnSelect` design is clean. However, there are a few real problems. The audience field sets `defaultOperator: 'is any of'`, which is not a valid operator key (the enum is `is_any_of`). The shared i18n defaults for the add-button label are now empty strings, so the Stats button is icon-only with no accessible name. The single-select path in the non-inline popover lost its `handleClose()` call, so the search text is no longer reset there. Two Tailwind classes (`!animation-none`) do nothing in Tailwind 3.4, and replacing `w-[200px]` with `field.className || 'w-[200px]'` drops the default width for any className that does not set one. No tests were added for any of the new behavior.
structured_output.verdictRationale: The wrong operator key on the audience filter is a functional bug in a core filter path, and the icon-only add button with empty i18n defaults removes the control's accessible name. Both should be fixed before merge. The remaining items (dropped search reset on single-select, no-op animation classes, width fallback, `var`, missing tests) are medium/low and can follow in the same change.

architecture.overview:
The Stats analytics page builds a list of filter field configs in `stats-filter.tsx` (UTM, source, post, audience) and hands them to the shared `Filters` component in `apps/shade/src/components/ui/filters.tsx`. `Filters` renders the add-filter button and popover. Selecting a field opens `SelectOptionsPopover` in inline mode, which emits values through `onChange` into `addFilterWithOption`, and that updates the parent filter array. Each field's `defaultOperator` and `hideOperatorSelect` decide what operator a new filter is created with and how it is displayed.

This PR adds a per-field `autoCloseOnSelect` flag so multiselect popovers can close after a pick, adds `selectedOptionsClassName` usage on the Stats fields to hide option icons in the trigger, widens the post popover, and changes the add button to an icon-only control. It also tightens shared visual defaults (padding, popover animation classes) that every consumer of `Filters` inherits.
steps: Entry point: `StatsFilter` in `stats-filter.tsx` builds `groupedFields` (UTM, source, post, audience) and renders `<Filters>` with `size='sm'`, a `FunnelPlus` icon, and empty button text.

Inside `Filters`, the add button falls back to `DEFAULT_I18N.addFilter`, which this PR changes to an empty string. Selecting a field with `type` `select` or `multiselect` opens `SelectOptionsPopover` with `inline={true}`.

In `SelectOptionsPopover`, a multiselect pick now calls `onClose` (or `handleClose`) when `autoCloseOnSelect` is set. The `onClose` callback resets `addFilterOpen` and `selectedFieldKeyForOptions`. Single-select picks in the non-inline popover (used by `FilterValueSelector` when editing an existing chip) no longer call `handleClose`.
New filters take their operator from `field.defaultOperator`. The audience field is changed to `'is any of'`, but the operator enum for multiselect is `is_any_of`, so the value must match that key.

Styling changes apply to all `Filters` consumers: `sm` input padding, `self-stretch` on the hidden operator box, and `!animation-none` / `!duration-0` on popover content. The popover width now comes from `field.className` only, not as a default fallback.

findings.title: Audience filter uses invalid operator key 'is any of'
findings.fixPrompt: In `apps/stats/src/views/Stats/components/stats-filter.tsx`, the audience field config (around line 453) sets `defaultOperator: 'is any of'`. The multiselect operator keys in `apps/shade/src/components/ui/filters.tsx` (around line 800) use snake_case, so the value should be `'is_any_of'`. Better, remove the explicit `defaultOperator` so the built-in multiselect default (line ~1977) applies. Check that no other config in this file uses display labels as operator values.

findings.title: Icon-only add button with empty i18n defaults has no accessible name
findings.body:
`DEFAULT_I18N.addFilter` and `addFilterTitle` are now `''` (filters.tsx lines 105 and 122). The Stats call passes `addButtonText={filters.length ? '' : ''}` (line 498), which is always `''`. The button renders `{addButtonIcon || <Plus />}{addButtonText || mergedI18n.addFilter}`, so it shows only the `FunnelPlus` icon. The `title` attribute is also empty.

The result is a button with no visible label, no `title`, and no `aria-label`. Screen readers announce it as an unnamed button, and sighted users lose the 'Add filter' affordance. The ternary is also dead code.

The default change is global. Any other `Filters` consumer that relied on the English defaults now gets an unlabeled button.

::diff{file="apps/stats/src/views/Stats/components/stats-filter.tsx" lines="495-501"}

::callout{type="security"}
This is an accessibility regression, not a security issue. The control needs a name.

Prefer keeping `'Add filter'` as the default and passing a visible label for Stats, or adding `aria-label` to the button. Remove the always-empty ternary.
findings.fixPrompt: Restore a non-empty accessible name for the filter add button. In `apps/shade/src/components/ui/filters.tsx`, `DEFAULT_I18N.addFilter` and `addFilterTitle` (around lines 105 and 122) were changed from 'Add filter' to ''; restore them, or add an `aria-label` on the button near line 2070. In `apps/stats/src/views/Stats/components/stats-filter.tsx` around line 498, replace the always-empty `addButtonText={filters.length ? '' : ''}` with a real label or remove it, and keep the icon-only design only if an `aria-label` is supplied. Match the existing i18n pattern used by the other props.

findings.title: Single-select path no longer resets search text on close
findings.fixPrompt: In `apps/shade/src/components/ui/filters.tsx`, the non-inline available-items `onSelect` in `SelectOptionsPopover` (around lines 1276-1277) calls `onChange` and then `setOpen(false)` for single-select, but no longer calls `handleClose()`. This means the `setSearchInput('')` added to `handleClose` (around line 1051) never runs on this path. Restore `handleClose()` in that else-branch, or call `setSearchInput('')` there too. Keep the `onClose` behavior the same as before this PR.

findings.title: Tailwind '!animation-none' class does nothing
findings.body:
`data-[state=closed]:!animation-none` is repeated on three `PopoverContent` classNames. Tailwind 3.4 (the version in `apps/shade/package.json`) has no `animation-*` utility. The animation utility is `animate-none`. So the class is never generated and the popover close animation is not disabled.

`!duration-0` is a real utility, so the duration half does something. The `animation-none` half was clearly meant to suppress the animation, and since it silently fails, the intended no-flicker close is not what ships. The same string is copy-pasted in three places, so a fix needs to touch all of them.

::diff{file="apps/shade/src/components/ui/filters.tsx" lines="1203-1206"}

If the goal is to suppress the close animation, use `data-[state=closed]:!animate-none` (and verify the class is generated in the Tailwind build), or drop the classes if they are not needed.
findings.fixPrompt: Three `PopoverContent` className strings in `apps/shade/src/components/ui/filters.tsx` (around lines 1204, 1644, and 2081) include `data-[state=closed]:!animation-none`. That is not a Tailwind 3.4 utility, so it generates no CSS. Replace it with the valid `data-[state=closed]:!animate-none` if the goal is to disable the close animation, and confirm the class is emitted in the built CSS. Otherwise remove it. Keep `!duration-0` only if it is needed. Apply the same change to all three sites.

findings.title: Custom popover className now drops the default width
findings.body:
The width logic changed from `cn('w-[200px] p-0', field.className)` to `cn('p-0 ...', field.className || 'w-[200px]')`. The default width is now used only when `className` is falsy. Any field that sets `className` without a width class (for example `'min-w-0'` or `'mx-2'`) gets an auto-width popover.

At the Filters level (line 2082), `selectedFieldForOptions?.className || popoverContentClassName || 'w-[200px]'` makes the field's className win outright, so a `popoverContentClassName` is ignored whenever the field also sets `className`. The Stats post field sets both to `'w-80'`, so it happens to be fine today, but the next consumer will hit this.

::diff{file="apps/shade/src/components/ui/filters.tsx" lines="1200-1212"}

Keep the default width as a base class and let the custom value override it, for example with `cn('w-[200px] p-0', field.className)` as before, or detect width classes explicitly. Apply the same approach to the Filters-level `PopoverContent`.
findings.fixPrompt: In `apps/shade/src/components/ui/filters.tsx`, the `SelectOptionsPopover` `PopoverContent` (around line 1205) uses `field.className || 'w-[200px]'`, which drops the default width whenever a custom className is set without a width. Restore a default width base class and let `field.className` override it, as the code did before this PR (`cn('w-[200px] p-0', field.className)`). Make the same change in the Filters-level `PopoverContent` around line 2082, where `selectedFieldForOptions?.className || popoverContentClassName || 'w-[200px]'` lets one value silently replace the other. Keep the Stats post field's `w-80` working.

findings.title: Inline auto-close skips the search reset used by the non-inline path
findings.fixPrompt: In `apps/shade/src/components/ui/filters.tsx`, the inline multiselect `onSelect` in `SelectOptionsPopover` (around lines 1134-1137) calls `onClose?.()` for `autoCloseOnSelect`, but the non-inline path (around line 1273) calls `handleClose()`, which also clears `searchInput`. Make both paths use the same close behavior, either by calling a shared helper that clears the search and then calls `onClose`, or by calling `setSearchInput('')` before `onClose?.()` in the inline branch.

findings.title: Use const instead of var in multiselect handler
findings.fixPrompt: In `apps/shade/src/components/ui/filters.tsx`, the multiselect branch of the inline `SelectOptionsPopover` `onSelect` (around line 1125) was changed from `const newValues` to `var newValues`. Change it back to `const`, matching the non-inline branch around line 1264.

findings.title: New filter behavior has no test coverage
findings.fixPrompt: Add tests for the Filters component in `apps/shade/src/components/ui/filters.tsx`. Cover (1) a multiselect field with `autoCloseOnSelect: true` that closes after one pick, (2) a single-select pick that clears the search text, and (3) that the Stats audience field produces an operator matching the multiselect operator enum (`is_any_of`) rather than a display label. Follow the rendering pattern already used in `filters.stories.tsx`.

findings.title: Auto-close is opt-in and reuses existing hooks
findings.body:
The `autoCloseOnSelect` flag is a small, opt-in config on `FilterFieldConfig`, with a comment explaining it overrides the multiselect default of staying open. It leaves other fields unchanged. The Stats side reuses the existing `selectedOptionsClassName` prop to hide icon chips on UTM and source fields, so no new shade API was needed for that.

::code{file="apps/shade/src/components/ui/filters.tsx" lines="747-752"}
